patients.summary: Unemployed man in his mid-40s living alone in Westhampton with severe alcohol use disorder, chronic calcific pancreatitis and thiamine deficiency who joins in 2021. Over 2023 he has a hernia repair complicated by delirium tremens, parotid sialadenosis, high-output and then alcoholic systolic heart failure from a femoral AV fistula and cardiomyopathy, and a pancreatic cyst; later a pseudocyst and Wernicke encephalopathy reach the chart only as outside records.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
44M new to the practice. No regular physician for several years.

History: Drinks about six beers a day and has for roughly eighteen years. Has tried to cut down more than once on his own, never lasted. No seizures or DTs that he knows of. Was admitted at an outside hospital for pancreatitis; told there it was the chronic calcified kind with repeat flares, had a tube through the nose for a few days, and was told his B1 was low. Brought the discharge sheet, which lists pancrelipase with meals, omeprazole, thiamine and a multivitamin. Admits he takes them when he remembers, enzymes maybe half of meals. No belly pain now. Smokes a pack a day, started in his late twenties. Used IV drugs years ago, nothing in a long time. Unemployed, lives by himself.

PSH: NG tube during the pancreatitis stay. No operations.
Family: father had a drinking problem and cirrhosis. Mother has high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes. An uncle on his father's side had a heart attack young.
Meds: pancrelipase 36,000 lipase-unit capsule with meals, omeprazole 20 daily, thiamine 100 daily, OTC multivitamin daily.
Allergies: none to medications.

Exam: pleasant, smells of smoke. Vitals in flowsheet. HEENT unremarkable. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. No edema. Neuro grossly nonfocal, gait steady.

Screens: AUDIT-C 10. PHQ-2 1.

A/P
1. Alcohol use disorder, severe. Talked about where this leads given his pancreas and his father. Offered addiction medicine referral; he would like to try on his own first. Told him never to stop cold at home without calling us.
2. Chronic calcific pancreatitis. Quiet today. Enzymes with every meal and snack, not just when he feels like it. Continue PPI.
3. Thiamine deficiency history. Keep taking B1 and the multivitamin.
4. Tobacco. Not ready to quit. Will keep asking.
5. Health maintenance: hep C antibody today given past IV use. CMP, CBC.
Follow up 3-4 months. Flu shot next month when stock arrives.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Neil, your blood counts, kidney and liver numbers came back fine, and the hepatitis C test was negative. Keep up the enzymes and the B1. See you in a few months.

documents.title: Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
45 y/o for his yearly visit. Feels at baseline. Mentions a lump in the left groin for maybe two months, pops out when he lifts or coughs and goes back when he lies down. No pain to speak of, no nausea, bowels normal.

Social: same drinking, same pack a day. Lives alone.
Screens: AUDIT-C 10, PHQ-2 0.

Exam: general well. Eyes, ears, throat normal. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Left inguinal bulge with cough, reduces easily, nontender, no skin change. Right side without hernia. Testes normal. Extremities without edema. Skin unremarkable.

Assessment/plan:
- Left inguinal hernia, reducible. Surgery referral for repair. Went over warning signs (stuck, painful, vomiting) that mean ER.
- Colon cancer screening at 45: FIT kit given.
- Tdap and flu given.
- AUD and tobacco: counseled; no change in readiness.
- Labs: CMP, CBC.
RTC after surgical consult.

documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Outside general surgery group. Date of visit: 11/01/2022.
Referred for: left groin bulge.

HPI: 45 year old man with a left groin bulge for several months, worse with straining, reduces on its own. No obstructive symptoms.
PMH per referral: chronic pancreatitis. Meds: pancrelipase, omeprazole, thiamine, multivitamin. Allergies: NKDA. Smokes.

Exam: reducible left inguinal hernia, no tenderness, no signs of incarceration. Right groin normal.

Impression: symptomatic reducible left inguinal hernia.
Plan: open left inguinal hernia repair with mesh. Scheduling to contact the patient with a date. Smoking cessation advised before surgery.

Thank you for the referral.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in because his face looks puffy to him. Says both cheeks have filled out over about four months, mostly in front of the ears. Not painful, doesn't change with meals. No fever. No dental pain. Hernia surgery is booked for early February with the surgeons.

Exam: symmetric fullness over both parotid areas, soft, nontender, no warmth or redness. Mouth without lesions. No neck nodes. Thyroid normal.

A/P: bilateral painless parotid enlargement. In a heavy drinker this is most often benign gland enlargement, but it deserves an ENT look. Referral placed. Discussed again how alcohol plays into this. Wished him well with the surgery; told him to be honest with the surgeons about how much he drinks.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
Regional hospital, inpatient medicine. Admitted 02/09/2023. Discharged 02/16/2023.

Reason for admission: elective open repair of a left inguinal hernia with mesh, done 02/09 without complication. Medicine consulted on post-op day 2.

Course: The patient told the surgical team before the operation that he had no medical problems and took no medicines. On the first post-op day he was calm. On the morning of post-op day 2 (02/11) he became restless and shaky, paced the room, kept asking to go home and snapped at staff when asked questions. He knew his name but not the place or date and said he could see spiders on the wall. T 37.3 C, BP 168/102, HR 122. Sweating with a fine tremor. Incision clean, no redness or drainage.

On closer history from the patient and his outside pharmacy he drinks about six beers a day, his last drink the night before surgery, and he carries a history of chronic calcific pancreatitis and low thiamine, with fills for pancrelipase, omeprazole and thiamine.

Diagnosis: alcohol withdrawal delirium (delirium tremens).
Treatment: transferred to a monitored bed, symptom-triggered IV lorazepam by withdrawal scale, IV thiamine before glucose and then daily, fluids and electrolyte repletion. Delirium cleared over about 72 hours; benzodiazepine weaned off by 02/15. Oriented and steady at discharge.

Discharge medications: pancrelipase 36,000 lipase units with meals, omeprazole 20 mg daily, thiamine 100 mg daily, multivitamin daily. No benzodiazepine at discharge.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP within 2 weeks; surgery clinic for wound check. Strongly advised to stop drinking under medical supervision only.

documents.title: Patient update after hospital stay
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called to let us know he had the hernia surgery on the 9th and then "went into the DTs" two days later, spent a week in. Home since Thursday. Incision healing, no fever. Not drinking since discharge, he says. No shakes now. Has an ENT appointment Friday. Hospital paperwork not sent to us; he doesn't have a copy. Records request faxed to the hospital. Post-hospital visit booked with PCP 3/7.

documents.title: Otolaryngology Consultation
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Outside otolaryngology practice. Date of visit: 02/24/2023.
Reason for referral: bilateral facial swelling.

History: 45-year-old man seen a week after a hospital stay for alcohol withdrawal delirium. About half a year of gradually fuller cheeks on both sides, painless. No recent infections, no fevers, no weight loss. Drinks about six beers daily, many years. Out of work, lives by himself.
Meds: pancrelipase, omeprazole, thiamine, multivitamin. NKDA.

Exam: vitals unremarkable. Both parotid glands enlarged, soft and nontender, skin over them normal without warmth or redness. Parotid duct openings clean, no stone felt and no pus expressed. Mucosa dry; no oral lesions; dentition without caries. Facial nerve intact. No cervical adenopathy.

Labs today: serum amylase and lipase normal. SS-A and SS-B antibodies negative. HIV screen nonreactive.

Impression: bilateral parotid sialadenosis, most likely from chronic alcohol use. No sign of Sjogren syndrome, infection or a mass.
Plan: no procedure needed. Reduction of alcohol is the treatment. Hydration, sugar-free lozenges for dryness. Return as needed.

Thank you for allowing me to see him.

events.reason: hospital follow-up; shortness of breath and leg swelling

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia, rate 106. Normal axis. Normal intervals. No ST elevation or depression. No Q waves.

documents.title: Post-hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after the hernia repair admission that turned into alcohol withdrawal delirium on POD2. Hospital summary still not here; history from him and the ENT letter, which arrived yesterday (parotid sialadenosis, Sjogren antibodies and HIV negative).

He says he has had one or two beers a day since getting home, down from six. No shakes, no confusion.

New today: when asked, admits he has been getting winded with stairs and walking for months now, more tired than he used to be, and his ankles and shins swell by night. No chest pain. Sleeps flat.

Exam: BP 104/64, HR 106 regular. Afebrile. Thin. Incision healed. Lungs clear. Heart tachycardic, regular. Pitting edema both lower legs. Parotids full bilaterally, nontender.
ECG: sinus tach 106, no acute changes.

A/P
1. Exertional dyspnea, fatigue, bilateral edema with resting tachycardia in a heavy drinker: worried about the heart. Cardiology referral, asked for soon. CMP and CBC today. ER if short of breath at rest or chest pain.
2. Delirium tremens, resolved. Any future attempt to quit has to be supervised. He agrees to call us first.
3. Sialadenosis per ENT. Alcohol is the fix.
4. Pancreatitis quiet. Same meds.

documents.body: Discharge summary from the February surgical admission received by fax in response to our 2/20 request. Filed to the admission and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group. Date of visit: 04/14/2023.
Referred by: primary care for dyspnea and edema.

HPI: 45-year-old man, recently hospitalized for alcohol withdrawal delirium after a hernia operation, then seen by ENT for parotid sialadenosis. Six months of steadily worse breathlessness with exertion and fatigue. No chest pain, no palpitations, no fainting.
History: alcohol use disorder, chronic calcific pancreatitis, thiamine deficiency. Prior IV drug use years ago, injecting in the left groin.
Meds: pancrelipase, omeprazole, thiamine, multivitamin. NKDA. Smokes 1 ppd.

Exam: BP 100/60, HR 110, SpO2 97% RA. JVP elevated. Loud continuous machinery murmur over the left groin, with a palpable thrill. Heart tachycardic, regular. 3+ pitting edema of both legs.

Data: Hgb 13.5, WBC 7.5, Plt 250, Cr 1.0, BNP 550.
CXR today: enlarged heart, increased pulmonary vascular markings.

Impression: high-output heart failure from an acquired left femoral arteriovenous fistula, a consequence of old groin injection. Volume overloaded.
Plan: start furosemide 40 mg each morning. Transthoracic echocardiogram, to be scheduled. Daily weights. Low-salt diet. Alcohol cessation advised. Return in about 4 months with echo, sooner if worse.

Thank you for this referral.

documents.title: BMP after furosemide start
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Cardiology started furosemide 40 daily on 4/14 (letter 4/24). Two-week BMP: sodium, potassium and kidney function fine. He says the swelling is down some. Continue.

documents.title: Abdominal pain
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt calling with upper belly pain about a week, dull, goes through to his back, worse some evenings. Not vomiting. No fever. Eating less. Not the same as his old bad flare, he says. Offered ER if severe; prefers to come in. Booked tomorrow 11:00 with PCP.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: epigastric pain in chronic calcific pancreatitis, weight loss

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
About one week of steady dull epigastric pain into the back, with spells where it gets worse. Appetite down. Weight 73 kg, five kilos lighter than his usual 78. No vomiting, no fever. Stools unchanged. Still drinking some most days. Breathing better on the furosemide.

Exam: afebrile, vitals in flowsheet. Not jaundiced. Abdomen soft with mild epigastric tenderness, no rebound or guarding, no mass felt. Legs with less swelling than in March.

A/P: epigastric pain with weight loss in chronic calcific pancreatitis. Not sick enough for the ER today. Abdominal ultrasound this week and GI referral. Enzymes with every meal. Return precautions given.

reports.text: Complete abdominal ultrasound. Liver normal in size and echotexture without focal lesion. Gallbladder without stones or wall thickening. Common bile duct normal caliber. A 6 cm cystic lesion lies adjacent to the pancreas and contains internal debris. Pancreas otherwise partially obscured by bowel gas. Spleen normal in size. Both kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis. Abdominal aorta normal in caliber. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: 6 cm cystic lesion adjacent to the pancreas with internal debris.

documents.title: Ultrasound result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: 6 cm cyst next to the pancreas with debris in it. In his setting most likely a pseudocyst. GI appointment already set for 6/23; forwarded the report. Called pt, reviewed, he will keep the appointment. ER if fever or pain worsens.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology group. Date of visit: 06/23/2023.
Reason: epigastric pain; cystic lesion on ultrasound.

HPI: 45-year-old man with chronic calcific pancreatitis and alcohol use disorder, recently admitted for withdrawal delirium and newly followed by cardiology for high-output heart failure. Three weeks of a dull, constant upper abdominal ache through to the back with intermittent worse spells. Eating less; about 5 kg down since his pancreatitis admission. No fever, no chills, no vomiting.
Meds: pancrelipase, omeprazole, thiamine, furosemide, multivitamin. NKDA.

Exam: vitals stable. Mild epigastric tenderness, no rebound, no guarding.
Labs: Hgb 13.2, WBC 9.0, amylase 120 U/L (ref 30-110), lipase 140 U/L (ref 0-160).
Imaging: outside ultrasound 6/16 reviewed, 6 cm peripancreatic cystic collection with debris.

Assessment: chronic calcific pancreatitis with a peripancreatic cystic lesion, most consistent with a pseudocyst. He is not obstructed or infected and the pain is tolerable, so no drainage now.
Plan: dietary management of chronic pancreatitis - small frequent low-fat meals, enzymes with every meal and snack, adequate protein, complete abstinence from alcohol. Continue pancrelipase and omeprazole. Call if pain escalates, fever, vomiting or early fullness.

Thank you for the referral.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
GI letter in: the cyst is probably a pseudocyst, they are watching it, diet plan and enzymes, no alcohol. Pain eased to a background ache. Weight still 73, eating one real meal a day plus snacks, often skips enzymes with snacks. Drinking 2-4 beers most days.

Exam: lean. Abdomen soft, minimal epigastric tenderness. Legs trace swelling.

A/P
1. Protein-calorie malnutrition: weight loss of about 5 kg with poor intake on top of pancreatic insufficiency and drinking. Added to problem list. Dietitian referral. Protein shakes between meals, enzymes with them too.
2. Pancreatic cyst, GI following.
3. High-output HF on furosemide, cardiology in August with echo.
4. AUD. Same conversation.
Labs today: CMP, CBC, Mg. 2 months.

conditions.label: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily with food

reports.text: Left ventricle is dilated with globally reduced systolic function. Visual ejection fraction 35%. No regional wall motion abnormality beyond the global hypokinesis. Right ventricle normal in size with preserved function. Atria normal in size. Valves structurally normal without significant stenosis or regurgitation. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Dilated left ventricle with reduced systolic function, ejection fraction 35%.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group. Date of visit: 08/18/2023.

Interval: seen in April for dyspnea attributed to his femoral fistula and started on furosemide. Now short of breath walking to the corner store, ankles puff up by evening, waking up breathless at night and propping himself on two pillows. No chest pain, fever, cough or palpitations. Still drinking several beers daily, about 20 years.
Meds: furosemide 40 daily, pancrelipase, omeprazole, thiamine, multivitamin. NKDA.

Exam: BP 104/70, HR 108. Apical impulse displaced out to the anterior axillary line. Low-pitched extra sound just after S2, consistent with an S3. No cardiac murmur. Fine crackles at both bases. Trace ankle edema.

Echo today: dilated LV, globally reduced systolic function, EF 35%.

Impression: alcoholic dilated cardiomyopathy with chronic systolic heart failure, NYHA class II-III, in addition to the fistula-related high-output physiology.
Plan: start lisinopril 10 mg daily, carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily and spironolactone 25 mg daily; continue furosemide 40 mg. BMP in 2-3 weeks via PCP. Total abstinence from alcohol is the most important treatment. Return in one year with echo, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Pharmacy call about new fills
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacist called to check an interaction question: pt filled lisinopril 10, carvedilol 12.5 BID and spironolactone 25 on 8/19 from his cardiologist, and they wanted to confirm we were aware given potassium with ACE inhibitor plus spironolactone. We had no letter from cardiology yet. Told pharmacist PCP will arrange a BMP. Note left for PCP; cardiology office called for the visit note.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Cardiology letter not received yet despite our call; per patient and pharmacy, echo showed a weak, enlarged heart and he was started on lisinopril, carvedilol and spironolactone on top of furosemide. Taking them most days. A little lightheaded standing quickly the first week, better now. Breathing somewhat easier, still uses two pillows some nights. Drinking 3-4 beers a day.

Exam: BP and HR in flowsheet, soft pressure as expected. Lungs clear today. Heart regular, no murmur heard at the precordium. Trace ankle edema.

A/P: HF with reduced EF, alcoholic cardiomyopathy per cardiology, on four drugs. BMP today for potassium and kidney function on ACE + spironolactone. Medication list updated from pharmacy fill data. Weigh daily, call if up 1 kg overnight or 2 kg in a week. Alcohol: this is the thing that could let the heart recover. He listened. Flu shot next month at a nurse visit.

documents.title: BMP result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Neil - potassium and kidney numbers are normal on the new heart pills. Keep taking all of them. We'll recheck in a few months.

documents.title: Cardiology note received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: August cardiology note and echo report finally received after second request. Filed. Routed to PCP to reconcile; matches what we already updated from pharmacy.

procedures.procedure: Preventive visit, established patient, 40-64

documents.title: Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
46M, yearly visit. A busy year: hernia repair with DTs in Feb, ENT for parotid swelling, cardiology twice (high-output HF from the old femoral AV fistula, then alcoholic cardiomyopathy EF 35%), GI for a pancreatic cyst. Weight back up a little to 74.5. Says he can walk to the store now without stopping, still tires on hills. Two pillows. Drinking about four beers a day. Smoking a pack.

Screens: AUDIT-C 10, PHQ-2 1.
Exam: thin. Parotids full bilaterally. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Continuous bruit over the left groin. Trace ankle edema. Abdomen soft, nontender.

Plan: CMP, CBC, lipid panel. FIT kit for this year. Vaccines done in October. Meds unchanged: furosemide 40, lisinopril 10, carvedilol 12.5 BID, spironolactone 25, pancrelipase with meals, omeprazole 20, thiamine 100, OTC multivitamin. Smoking and drinking counseling, he is listening more than he used to but no plan. Follow-up March.

documents.title: FIT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: FIT negative again. Next kit in a year. Letter mailed.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Doing about the same. Walks short distances fine, rests on the hill to his road. Weight steady. No belly flares, the background ache comes and goes. Enzymes most meals. Drinks 3-5 a day. Says he wants to quit this spring.

Exam: vitals charted. Lungs clear. Regular rhythm. Groin bruit unchanged. Trace edema.

A/P: HFrEF stable on furosemide, lisinopril, carvedilol, spironolactone. Pancreatitis and cyst without change in symptoms. Malnutrition: weight holding. He brought up quitting; went over why he must not stop on his own after what happened last February, and that we can set up supervised withdrawal. He'll think it over. 90-day refills sent.

documents.title: Quitting
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I'm going to stop drinking starting this weekend. Going to do it myself this time, I don't want to go anywhere.

documents.title: RE: Quitting
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Neil, I'm really glad you want to stop. Please don't stop all at once at home. Last time you stopped suddenly you became very sick, and it can happen again. Let me get you to addiction medicine this week for a supervised plan, or come in and we will work it out together. Can I put the referral in?

documents.title: RE: Quitting
documents.author: patient
documents.body: No referral. I'll cut down slow then.

documents.title: Update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Made it about 2 weeks with 1 or 2 a day then back to where I was. Not shaky. Just letting you know.

documents.title: RE: Update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me. Two weeks cutting down is real progress. The offer for addiction medicine stays open. See you on the 25th.

documents.title: No-show
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: No-show for 9:20. Portal reminder sent to reschedule.

reports.text: Left ventricle dilated with global hypokinesis. Ejection fraction 30%. Right ventricle normal in size and function. Valves without significant disease. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Dilated left ventricle with reduced systolic function, ejection fraction 30%.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group. Date of visit: 08/08/2024.

One-year follow-up. Over the last few months more breathless with exertion and more leg swelling. Occasional palpitations. Needs pillows to sleep. He tried to stop drinking a few months ago, did not hold. Drinking about 20 years.
Meds: furosemide 40 daily, lisinopril 10 daily, carvedilol 12.5 BID, spironolactone 25 daily, pancrelipase, omeprazole, thiamine. NKDA.

Exam: BP 105/68, P 95, RR 20. JVD present. Apical impulse displaced. S3 gallop. Crackles at both bases. 2+ pitting edema of the legs.

Echo today: dilated LV, EF 30%.

Impression: alcoholic cardiomyopathy, chronic systolic HF, symptoms worse with ongoing alcohol use. Femoral AV fistula as before.
Plan: continue current regimen. Abstinence is essential. Low salt, daily weights. Return in one year.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Missed June. Cardiology note from 8/8 reviewed: EF now 30%, regimen unchanged. He feels about the same as in spring, maybe a bit more winded. Back to 4-6 beers. Still a pack a day.

Exam: soft BP, HR in the 90s per flowsheet. JVP not clearly elevated sitting up. Lungs with few basilar crackles. Regular rhythm. Trace to 1+ ankle edema.

A/P: HFrEF, worse EF with ongoing drinking. Taking his four heart meds. BMP and Mg today. Reviewed fluid and salt. Alcohol and tobacco again; still no plan he will commit to. Flu and COVID at a nurse visit in October.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine check. Winter has been quiet: no ER visits, no flares of the pancreas, the ache under the ribs is there on and off. Breathing no worse than the fall. Weight about 74. Taking heart pills and B1 daily, enzymes most meals. Drinking 4-6 most days. Pack a day.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Parotids full. Lungs clear but for a few crackles at the right base. Heart regular. Groin bruit left. 1+ ankle edema.

A/P
- HFrEF / alcoholic cardiomyopathy, EF 30% in August: same regimen, cardiology again in summer.
- Chronic calcific pancreatitis with pancreatic cyst: symptoms stable; GI as needed.
- Malnutrition: weight steady about 74.
- AUD severe, tobacco: counseled; supervised detox offer stands.
CMP and CBC drawn today. Follow up in 4 months; front desk to call with a date.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Neil, Friday's bloodwork came back okay: kidneys, potassium, liver tests and blood counts all within range. Please call to set up the spring visit.

documents.title: Scheduling outreach
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called to book 4-month follow-up. Left message. Second message sent through portal.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requests 90-day refills of all heart meds, omeprazole, thiamine and pancrelipase. PCP approved a 30-day supply with a note on the label to schedule a visit. Pt has not responded to scheduling calls.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Pancreas: coarse calcifications throughout the gland. A well-circumscribed fluid collection with a defined wall measuring 7 cm lies at the pancreatic body, consistent with a pseudocyst. No peripancreatic fat stranding. Liver, gallbladder and spleen unremarkable. No biliary dilatation. Kidneys without hydronephrosis. Bowel without obstruction. No free fluid or free air. Postsurgical change of left inguinal hernia repair.
reports.conclusion: 7 cm pancreatic pseudocyst at the body of the pancreas; calcifications of chronic calcific pancreatitis.

procedures.procedure: Emergency department visit, high MDM

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Seen 08/22/2025.

CC: upper abdominal fullness, 3 weeks.
HPI: 48-year-old man with chronic calcific pancreatitis and severe alcohol use disorder. For three weeks a dull upper abdominal discomfort and fullness, worse when he bends forward, and he fills up after a few bites. Similar problem in June 2023; it settled partly but was never entirely gone. Lost about 5 kg without trying. No fever, no yellowing, no vomiting blood, no change in bowel habits. Drinks often.
Meds per list: furosemide, lisinopril, carvedilol, spironolactone, pancrelipase, omeprazole, thiamine, multivitamin. NKDA.

Exam: T 37.1, P 92, BP 128/76, BMI 22. Looks tired, not toxic. Abdomen soft, mildly distended, tender firm fullness in the epigastrium.
Labs: amylase and lipase normal.
CT A/P with contrast: 7 cm pseudocyst at the pancreatic body, pancreatic calcifications.

Impression: symptomatic pancreatic pseudocyst in chronic pancreatitis.
Disposition: pain controlled, tolerating liquids. Discharged with urgent outpatient gastroenterology follow-up for drainage evaluation. Return for fever, vomiting, worsening pain or bleeding.

documents.body: Per PCP, called pt after ED visit. Says GI called him and he has a procedure coming up. Pain manageable. Encouraged him to book a visit with us; he will call after the GI procedure.

documents.body: Refill requests for heart meds and omeprazole. Overdue for visit since May. PCP approved 30 days and asked front desk to call. Message left.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
Regional hospital, inpatient medicine. Admitted 02/23/2026 through the emergency department. Discharged 03/09/2026.

Presentation: 48-year-old man with severe alcohol use disorder, chronic calcific pancreatitis with a pseudocyst treated by EUS-guided cystgastrostomy and stent in October 2025, alcoholic cardiomyopathy and prior withdrawal delirium. Brought in by ambulance after weeks of increasingly odd behavior, repeated falls and trouble walking. On arrival disoriented, with impaired horizontal eye movements, unable to stand without help.

Diagnosis: Wernicke encephalopathy.
Course: high-dose IV thiamine started in the ED before any glucose and continued three times daily, then tapered to oral. Withdrawal monitored. Course complicated on hospital day 3 by aspiration pneumonia, treated with IV ampicillin-sulbactam with a full recovery from the pneumonia. Orientation and eye movements improved over the stay; still needs help with walking at discharge.

Disposition: short-term rehabilitation facility.
Discharge medications: thiamine 100 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, carvedilol 12.5 mg BID, spironolactone 25 mg daily, pancrelipase with meals, omeprazole 20 mg daily, multivitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP after rehab discharge; cardiology and GI as scheduled. No alcohol.

documents.title: Discharge summary received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Discharge summary from a February-March 2026 admission received, unsolicited, almost five weeks after discharge. Filed and flagged for PCP. Our office was not notified of the admission at the time. GI procedure in October 2025 mentioned in it; no GI report on file.

documents.title: Patient call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called. Home from rehab since last week, says his thinking is "mostly back." Asking for refills. Reviewed: needs a visit, last seen January 2025. Offered next week; he wants to check on a ride first and will call back. 30-day refills approved by PCP. Pharmacy confirmed.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requests refills of furosemide, carvedilol, lisinopril, spironolactone, thiamine. No visit booked since April call. PCP approved 30 days; front desk asked to reach him for an appointment. Voicemail left.
